note: ep10 Short 2 (2026-11-13): the break-even and the life table only, about a minute, 9:16. Same model as nguyens/lines.json (plain checks, today's money). Race lines carry `month` = months since the 62nd birthday. Every spoken number is checked by tools/validate-ep10-story.mjs. The family are illustrations.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Uncle Tu just turned sixty-two. Social Security: *fourteen hundred* a month now, or *twenty-four hundred eighty* if he waits until seventy.

lines.speaker: T
lines.text: I take it now. Who knows if I'm still here at eighty?

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: In today's money: by seventy, taking it early has collected a hundred thirty-four thousand dollars. Waiting: zero.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Then the bigger check catches up, a thousand eighty dollars a month. A little past *eighty*, they're even.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: So, will he make it to eighty? Social Security's own table: of a hundred men who reach sixty-two, about *six in ten* do. On average, a man lives to about eighty-two.

lines.speaker: L
lines.text: And if he lives to ninety-five, waiting is ahead by about a hundred ninety thousand.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Waiting isn't a bet that you live long. It's insurance, in case you do. Would you take it at sixty-two, or wait? Tell me in the comments.
